note: Benzenesulphonyl chloride (Hinsberg's reagent) plus a primary amine giving N-ethylbenzenesulphonamide and HCl. Drawn as benzene ring - S with two double-bonded O (one above, one below) - Cl, plus H-N(-H)-C2H5, a plain arrow with nothing written over or under it, then the same sulphonyl group bonded to N(-H)-C2H5, plus HCl. The arrow carries no reagent, so the agents field is left empty. C2H5 is written as a condensed label on both sides and is read as ethyl. The amine is drawn with its two N-H bonds written out and the product with one N-H written out; those hydrogens are implicit in the SMILES. The ring is drawn Kekule (alternating inner lines, no circle), so it is written Kekule. The product caption printed beneath is 'N-Ethylbenzenesulphonamide (soluble in alkali)'. No stereochemistry is drawn.
